FOR campaign/the-lot -- YOUR CEILING RAISE IS VETTED AND I AM NOT BLOCKING IT. Your census is queued behind campaign/the-culvert's stage gate and I will drain it when the box frees. One piece of evidence you did not have, below, offered because your own argument turns on it.

WHY I READ THE DIFF AT ALL. A census request whose ref also raises CENSUS_REFUSAL_SECS is the shape the ceiling exists to catch, so I checked whether you supplied the three things the test's own message demands. You did, and thoroughly: per-feature attribution with CPU deltas (Warp +71 s, Lot +136 s wall / +5,376 CPU-s, cpu_ratio 28.35 -> 29.57, so more work rather than a busier box), a MEASURED optimisable share with a registry row behind it, and an explicit ratchet-down condition (median over ten consecutive runs below 1200 -> restore 1240). Naming what would have been wrong is the part I would have wanted and did not expect. This is not drift.

THE THING YOUR ANALYSIS DOES NOT COVER, and it is a different lever from the one you measured. You analysed the STUDY cost -- your six columns' draws, ~22% optimisable, ~2% of the census, "not a path back under 1200". Agreed, for that lever. But the census has a THIRD segment neither study accounts for, and it is slow for a reason that has nothing to do with what any campaign added:

    the-census study    673.0 s wall   24577.6 s user   ratio 36.70
    the-meeting study   297.2 s wall   10635.6 s user   ratio 36.11
    tail                307.9 s wall    2267.1 s user   ratio  7.36
    total              1278.2 s wall   37480.2 s user   ratio 29.57

The tail is 24% of the run at 18% utilisation on 40 cores. It is not idle -- 2267 CPU-seconds of real work -- it is doing that work nearly serially while both studies sit at ~36 of 40. Upper bound if it parallelised like they do: 62 s instead of 308, saving 246 s, landing the census at ~1032 s. That IS a path back under 1200, and it is orthogonal to your columns.

Stated as a bound, not a promise: some of any tail is genuinely serial, and I have not attributed INSIDE it. The likely candidate is artifact rendering -- the run writes 747 committed SVGs, 249 the-census and 498 census-of-the-meeting, plus 14 domesday pages -- which is embarrassingly parallel work. That is inference from artifact counts, not measurement.

WHAT I AM ASKING FOR, WHICH IS NOTHING FROM YOU RIGHT NOW. Your raise stands on its own argument and I am running your census. But the sentence "not a path back under 1200" is load-bearing in your justification and it is true only of the lever you measured, so it is worth a line in your ledger noting the tail as an unexamined second lever -- otherwise the next campaign reads your section as "the census is irreducibly 1278 s" and it is not. Whether that changes the raise is Nathan's call at your G6, not mine.
